slides.title:
Longevity is the
qualification.
slides.body:
Most food labels you meet in Korea rate hygiene, or a grade, or a guidebook's opinion. These two rate survival.

백년가게 — 'hundred-year shop' — has been run by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups with the Small Enterprise and Market Service since 2018. A small business needs thirty years or more in food service or retail even to apply. A panel then scores how sustainable it is, how its product and service stand up, and what it means to the neighbourhood.

There is a sister label for makers: 백년소공인, same idea, fifteen years in manufacturing. Workshops, not dining rooms.

slides.cta:
Two words, decades of evidence.
Save this for your next walk

caption:
Korea labels its survivors. Two schemes, two plaques, and both are worth knowing if you would rather eat somewhere that has held the same corner for decades.

The national one is 백년가게, 'hundred-year shop'. The Ministry of SMEs and Startups has run it with the Small Enterprise and Market Service since 2018. A small business needs thirty years or more in food service or retail even to apply; a panel then scores sustainability, product and service, and what the shop means locally. A sister label, 백년소공인, does the same for makers with fifteen years in manufacturing.

This year's cohort was announced in July 2026: 150 shops and 150 workshops, chosen from 747 applicants, about 2.5 to 1. That takes the running totals to 1,545 hundred-year shops and 1,053 hundred-year makers. Each gets a certification plaque for the door, a storyboard of the business's history, and preference in small-business lending.

Seoul runs its own, older and smaller. 오래가게 — a pun on 'a shop that lasts' — started in 2017 and is aimed squarely at visitors. Thirty years is the bar here too, across food, crafts and everyday neighbourhood trades. In September 2026 the city added fifteen restaurants in Gwangjin, Dongdaemun, Seongdong and Jungnang, picked from 1,731 public nominations and then verified on site, taking the citywide list to 150.

Using them is easy. The plaque hangs in plain sight, so the two words are worth memorising. Seoul says its 150 can be found by searching 오래가게 in Naver Map, and on the city's Smart Seoul Map. The national list is simply a government download: the agency publishes every designated shop's name, address and phone on data.go.kr, last updated 30 August 2026, with no usage restriction.

One caveat. Neither plaque is a review. Both reward longevity and local standing, not the best bowl of anything, and neither tells you today's opening hours.

Sources on the last slide. Research, not a visit, and no venue recommended here.
